Chapter 1: Rethinking Success and the Trap of Average Ambitions
Let’s take a moment to think about what success really means. For most of us, it’s a moving target—something we chase, but hardly ever stop to define in a clear or bold way.
The truth is, if we want to see real change in our results, we have to start by challenging the quiet assumptions that shape our ambitions. Have you ever noticed how easy it is to set goals that feel reasonable? Goals that are safe, or just a little better than where you are now?
It’s natural to want to avoid disappointment. But here’s the catch—playing it safe can quietly box in what’s actually possible for you.
Look around, and you’ll see tons of examples—people and companies alike—who have plenty of talent and put in the work, but somehow stay stuck right in the middle of the pack.
And it’s not usually because they’re missing brains or opportunity. What holds them back is an invisible ceiling—one built by average thinking.
When your goals are only a little bit above your current circumstances, the actions you take are going to be just as modest. That leads to a cycle where the only outcomes you get are, well, average. And over time, the gap between your potential and your reality just keeps getting wider.
Think about a runner who trains just enough to finish a race—not to win it. The difference in how they prepare, how they think, and the energy they bring is huge. It’s the same in life and work. If you approach things with the mindset of just “getting by” or “doing well enough,” you’ll never break through to something truly remarkable.
So, here’s the insight that changes everything: The size of your goal determines the scale of your actions. If your ambition is small, you’ll only invest so much energy and creativity. But when you set a goal that feels almost out of reach—something ten times bigger than you think is possible—you force your mind to stretch. Suddenly, you’re coming up with new strategies, and you’re tapping into reserves of effort you didn’t even know you had.
This is what the 10X principle is all about. Ordinary thinking and effort? They’ll only ever lead you to ordinary results. If you want to break free from the pull of mediocrity, you’ve got to set goals that are ten times bigger than what feels comfortable.
And no, it’s not about wishful thinking or empty bravado. It’s about choosing a target so compelling it actually demands a whole new level of commitment from you.
The truth is, the world doesn’t reward those who play it safe. Look at any field, and you’ll see the most successful people are the ones who refuse to settle for average. They treat success as a responsibility—not just to themselves, but to their families and communities too. By aiming higher, they open doors not just for themselves, but for everyone around them.
So, the real first step? Take a hard look at the beliefs that are shaping your ambition. Are you setting your sights based on what feels doable, or on what would truly transform your life and work? Are you willing to lean into discomfort for the sake of something extraordinary?
These are the questions that lay the foundation for everything else. Because once you start asking them, you’re already on your way to breaking out of the trap of average ambitions.
